newsitem.title: USA: Continental has merger potential - study.
newsitem.headline: Continental has merger potential - study.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc's pilots union on Monday said a study it commissioned shows that the Houston-based airline could eventually merge with another carrier, perhaps within the next 18 to 24 months.

The study, prepared by Salomon Brothers, forecast a rapid consolidation in the airline industry if the proposed alliance between British Airways Plc (BA) and AMR Corp's American Airlines was approved, said Len Nikolai, president of the Independent Association of Continental Pilots.

Continental, which had been in merger talks late last year with Delta Air Lines, said it had not seen a copy of the study and declined to comment. A spokeswoman emphasized that the airline was not in talks with any other airline.

The Salomon Brothers study suggested Continental would emerge as an attractive acquisition candidate because of its strong domestic and international route structure, solid financial situation, and relatively good relations between its management and employees, Nikolai said.
In January, Continental Chairman Gordon Bethune said he did expected to see a consolidation in the next year.
"A lot of this hinges on the BA-American code-sharing deal going through. That deal would precipitate further consolidation in the airline industry," Nikolai said.

The BA-American deal is contingent on the formation of a new "open skies" treaty between the U.S. and Britain. U.S. and British aviation officials have been negotiating an aviation pact for months. Talks were held last week in Washington, but no agreement was reached.

Recent strife between American Airlines with its pilots' union poses a further obstacle to the quick completion of the proposed BA alliance. A presidential board has been appointed to study the labor conflict and propose a solution.
Salomon Brothers representatives could not be reached for comment.
